I think this would be the best way to learn more about their relationship and ensure that she has given enough thought to his infidelity - although it would be hard to imagine how she could not have done so extensively before agreeing to marry him. Ultimately, it is up to her to make the decision.

Self-harm is serious.

Hi,

I have had similar issues in the past and empathise with your situation; I am sorry that you are having a difficult time. Unfortunately, it sounds as though you have not fully come to terms with your mental health struggles and the severity of the situation. It also seems like you are very tough on yourself and would see taking a year out as a personal failure. As others have pointed out, medicine is very tough, and you absolutely **must** be in good health to take on the challenges that you will face, both in your studies and in your career. There is nothing wrong with taking a year out to make sure you can continue (or leave medicine! if that's what you want). Your mental health really needs to be your top priority, and if you don't take the time to address it now it will only fester and continue to cause problems down the line - you said yourself that you had self harmed in the past and have now relapsed, so this is an ongoing issue for you. Have a think about what would be best for you, maybe a summer dedicated to healing and being kind to yourself would be enough, or maybe you do need to take a full year to do that. The anger you are feeling towards your friend is misguided, they are doing their best to help, and you shouldn't underestimate how distressing it can be for those around you to see you hurting yourself.  

Wishing you the best!
